title: Three kinds of count per clinic
prompt:
A group of physio clinics logs every appointment. After a visit the patient may leave a rating; if they don't, rating is NULL.

For every clinic, report how many appointments it had, how many of those got a rating, and how many different patients it saw.

- Columns: clinic (the clinic name), appointments, rated, unique_patients
- One row per clinic, including clinics with no appointments (all three counts 0)
- Any row order is fine
hints: Start from clinics so that clinics without appointments still appear. Which join keeps them?
count(*) counts rows, count(col) counts non-NULL values, count(DISTINCT col) counts different non-NULL values. After a LEFT JOIN an empty clinic still has one row.
LEFT JOIN appointments a ON a.clinic_id = c.id, GROUP BY c.id, c.name, and use count(a.id), count(a.rating), count(DISTINCT a.patient_id).

exercise.schema:
CREATE TABLE clinics (id int PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE appointments (id int PRIMARY KEY, clinic_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES clinics(id), patient_id int NOT NULL, rating int CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5));
exercise.starter:
-- Appointment counts per clinic
SELECT c.name AS clinic,
       count(*) AS appointments,
       count(*) AS rated,
       count(*) AS unique_patients
FROM clinics c
LEFT JOIN appointments a ON a.clinic_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
exercise.solution:
SELECT c.name AS clinic,
       count(a.id) AS appointments,
       count(a.rating) AS rated,
       count(DISTINCT a.patient_id) AS unique_patients
FROM clinics c
LEFT JOIN appointments a ON a.clinic_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

tests.name: two busy clinics
tests.seed:
INSERT INTO clinics VALUES (1, 'Northside'), (2, 'Harbor');
INSERT INTO appointments VALUES (1, 1, 100, 5), (2, 1, 100, NULL), (3, 1, 101, 4), (4, 2, 200, NULL);

tests.name: clinic with no appointments
tests.seed:
INSERT INTO clinics VALUES (1, 'Elm'), (2, 'Oak');
INSERT INTO appointments VALUES (1, 1, 10, 3);

hiddenTests.name: no ratings at all
hiddenTests.seed:
INSERT INTO clinics VALUES (1, 'Pine');
INSERT INTO appointments VALUES (1, 1, 7, NULL), (2, 1, 8, NULL);

hiddenTests.name: one patient many visits
hiddenTests.seed:
INSERT INTO clinics VALUES (1, 'Ash'), (2, 'Yew');
INSERT INTO appointments VALUES (1, 1, 5, 2), (2, 1, 5, 3), (3, 1, 5, 3), (4, 1, 5, NULL), (5, 2, 5, 1);

explanation: The LEFT JOIN keeps every clinic; a clinic with no appointments gets one row whose appointment columns are all NULL. count(*) counts that row and reports 1, which is the trap, while count(a.id) skips the NULL and reports 0. count(a.rating) counts only rated visits because aggregates ignore NULLs, and count(DISTINCT a.patient_id) collapses repeat visits. Grouping by c.id as well as the name keeps two clinics with the same name apart.
notes: count(DISTINCT ...) usually forces a sort or hash per group, so it is the most expensive of the three on large data. An index on appointments(clinic_id) helps when you only need a few clinics. Grouping by the primary key c.id lets Postgres accept other clinics columns in SELECT without listing them.
followUps: Add the average rating per clinic, rounded to 2 decimals, NULL when nobody rated.
What changes if two clinics share a name and you group only by name?
